name: Arabic, qəltu dialect of Dhalaʿ, Lahej province
catalog_citation: Vanhove, Martine. 1993. Note sur le dialecte qəltu de Dhalaʿ (province de Lahej, Yémen). Matériaux Arabes et Sudarabiques (MAS-GELLAS) Nouvelle Série 5: 165-190. Open copy: HAL halshs-00009746 (author typescript scan), https://shs.hal.science/halshs-00009746/…
catalog_locator: sec. 1.3 'Accentuation et structure syllabique', typescript pp. 7-8 (= HAL PDF pp. 8-9; published pagination approx. pp. 171-172); re-read during this reading …
catalog_quote: La place de l'accent à l'intérieur d'un mot est déterminée par la structure de la forme lexicale. L'accent tombe sur le premier groupe lourd à partir de la fin du mot, c'est-à-dire V̄C ou VCC : buṭū́n "ventres", lābᵊsā́t "revêtant (f. pl.)", dafā́tər "livres", lā́bisah "revêtant (f. sg.)", baqárti "ma vache", tegámmaʿū "ils rassemblèrent". S'il n'y a pas de groupe lourd, l'accent porte sur la première syllabe du mot : rúkab "genoux", kátabū "ils écrivirent", báqarah "une vache". La seule exception à la règle provient des verbes faibles du type gāʾ "venir" où les personnes de l'inaccompli qui ont une structure syllabique de type CVCV̄ sont accentuées sur la dernière syllabe : nigī́ "nous venons". [fn. 8:] Cette accentuation est similaire à celle donnée par Diem (1973:125) pour Rāḥideh dans la Hogariyah.

new_statements.translation: The position of the accent within a word is determined by the structure of the lexical form. The accent falls on the first heavy group counting from the end of the word, i.e. V̄C or VCC: buṭū́n 'bellies', lāb°sā́t 'wearing (f. pl.)', dafā́tər 'books', lā́bisah 'wearing (f. sg.)', baqárti 'my cow', tegámmaʿū 'they gathered'. If there is no heavy group, the accent falls on the first syllable of the word: rúkab 'knees', kátabū 'they wrote', báqarah 'a cow'. The only exception to the rule comes from weak verbs of the type gāʾ 'to come', where the imperfect persons with a CVCV̄ syllable structure are accented on the last syllable: nigī́ 'we come'.

Section "1.3. Accentuation et structure syllabique" starts at the foot of typescript p. 7 and the quoted passage is there word for word: "La place de l'accent à l'intérieur d'un mot est déterminée par la structure de la forme lexicale. L'accent tombe sur le premier groupe lourd à partir de la fin du mot, c'est-à-dire V̄C ou VCC : buṭū́n 'ventres', lāb°sā́t.., dafā́tər.., lā́bisah" (p. 7) continuing on p. 8 ".. baqárti⁷ 'ma vache', tegámmaʿū 'ils rass…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress the rightmost heavy sequence in the word, heavy = long vowel followed by a consonant (V̄C) or short vowel followed by two consonants (VCC), counted from the end (a word-final CVC or final long vowel does not attract stress: rúkab, kátabū); if the word contains no such sequence, stress the first syllable. Classic Arabic-dialect weight rule (rightmost superheavy/heavy sequence, else initial).
new_statements.exceptions: CVCV̄ imperfect forms of final-weak verbs (gāʾ 'come': nigī́ 'we come') take final stress. Fn. 7: construct-state feminines with vowel loss (baqárti) stressed as in western Ḥugariyya. Sec. 2.1: nouns that lost Classical final -ā are stressed on the first syllable (šítā 'winter', sémaʾ 'sky'); sec. 2.2: colour adjectives lengthen the vowel under stress (ḥ°mā́r 'red'). Fn. 8: 'Cette accentuation est similaire à celle donnée par Diem (1973:125) pour Rāḥideh dans la Hogariyah.'
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; examples are citation forms and suffixed word forms (baqárti, baqárt-ə-kom, tegámmaʿū); based on a corpus from one male speaker from Dhalaʿ recorded in Aden, winter 1991.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the dialect of Dhalaʿ (aḍ-Ḍāliʿ), Lahej province, former PDRY — a 'qəltu'-type highland dialect that Vanhove places as the southern continuation of Behnstedt's Ḥugariyya group (Taʿizz governorate) — inside the Taʿizzi-Adeni (acq / taiz1242) area; Glottolog lists no dialect-level glottocode for it. Data from a single male speaker recorded in Aden in 1991. Vanhove fn. 8 says the same accentuation holds for Rāḥida in the Ḥugariyya per Diem (1973:125), which ties it to Taʿizzi proper. Separately, the Shachmon & Faust 2026 abstract reports default FINAL stress for the Arabic of the Jews of Aden — a Judeo-Yemeni variety (Glottolog's Judeo-Yemeni Arabic languoid, code not verified here), not the Muslim Adeni koine; this should not be conflated with the Dhalaʿ rule.

readall_conflicts: One apparent conflict, across varieties rather than within one: the catalog's weight-sensitive rule (Vanhove 1993, Dhalaʿ qəltu: stress on the first heavy syllable from the end) versus the Shachmon & Faust 2026 abstract's 'default final stress' for the Arabic of the Jews of Aden. Both fall under Glottolog taiz1242 (Ta'izzi-Adeni), but they are distinct dialects (rural qəltu of Dhalaʿ vs. urban Jewish Aden), so the catalog entry as named ('qəltu dialect of Dhalaʿ') is not contradicted by it. The Shachmon & Faust claim rests on the abstract alone; the full text was not obtainable (De Gruyter AWS-WAF challenge on both html and pdf, HTTP 202 with no content, two attempts; Unpaywall lists no repository copy; no lingbuzz preprint).
